## `imsg`

iMessage client over Bluetooth MAP/PBAP

**Usage:** `imsg [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `send` — Send an SMS to a phone number
* `list` — List messages in a folder
* `get` — Fetch one message body by handle
* `delete` — Delete (or undelete) a message by handle
* `contacts` — Pull contacts from a phonebook
* `threads` — Group inbox and sent messages into conversation threads
* `sync` — Backfill the local store with all messages from the device since the last sync
* `unsync` — Stop using the local store for reads; synced data is preserved by default
* `folders` — List the MAP message folders on the device
* `hub` — Start the iroh hub on this machine and print the node key for spokes
* `spoke` — Manage spoke configuration for connecting to a remote hub
* `config` — Inspect or modify local configuration
* `broker` — Query the session broker
* `daemon` — Manage the persistent background broker (opt-in; required for GUI use)
* `completions` — Print a shell completion script to stdout, or install it directly

###### **Options:**

* `--hub` — Route MAP and PBAP connections through the iroh hub configured via `imsg spoke add`
* `--device <ADDR>` — Override the configured device MAC address (RFCOMM only)
* `--config <PATH>` — Explicit config file path, overriding the layered default search
* `-v`, `--verbose` — Increase logging verbosity
* `-q`, `--quiet` — Decrease logging verbosity



## `imsg send`

Send an SMS to a phone number

**Usage:** `imsg send <NUMBER> <MESSAGE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NUMBER>` — Recipient phone number
* `<MESSAGE>` — Message body



## `imsg list`

List messages in a folder

**Usage:** `imsg list [OPTIONS] [FOLDER]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<FOLDER>` — Folder to list; defaults to inbox

  Possible values:
  - `inbox`:
    Received messages
  - `sent`:
    Sent messages
  - `outbox`:
    Pending outbound messages
  - `deleted`:
    Deleted messages


###### **Options:**

* `--unread` — Only unread messages
* `-l`, `--long` — Show the raw MAP handle for each message (for use with `get`/`delete`)
* `--from <NUMBER>` — Filter by originating address
* `--since <DATE>` — Filter to messages at or after this MAP timestamp (`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS`)
* `--limit <N>` — Maximum number of entries to return
* `--offset <N>` — Skip the first N entries (pagination)



## `imsg get`

Fetch one message body by handle

**Usage:** `imsg get [OPTIONS] <HANDLE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<HANDLE>` — Message handle

###### **Options:**

* `--folder <FOLDER>` — Folder the handle lives in; defaults to inbox

  Possible values:
  - `inbox`:
    Received messages
  - `sent`:
    Sent messages
  - `outbox`:
    Pending outbound messages
  - `deleted`:
    Deleted messages

* `--mark-read` — Mark the message read after fetching



## `imsg delete`

Delete (or undelete) a message by handle

**Usage:** `imsg delete [OPTIONS] <HANDLE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<HANDLE>` — Message handle

###### **Options:**

* `--folder <FOLDER>` — Folder the handle lives in; defaults to inbox

  Possible values:
  - `inbox`:
    Received messages
  - `sent`:
    Sent messages
  - `outbox`:
    Pending outbound messages
  - `deleted`:
    Deleted messages

* `--undelete` — Restore a previously deleted message instead of deleting it



## `imsg contacts`

Pull contacts from a phonebook

**Usage:** `imsg contacts [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--list` — List handles/UIDs and names only, without full vCards
* `--get <KEY>` — Fetch a single contact: a PBAP handle live/via broker, or a cached UID once opted in (matches whatever `--list` just printed in that mode)
* `--lookup <NUMBER>` — Reverse-lookup a contact by phone number
* `--sync` — Refresh the local contacts cache from the device. No effect from `--raw`/`--limit`/ `--page`; always syncs the main phonebook regardless of `--path`
* `--path <PATH>` — Phonebook to read. No effect on `--sync` (always the main phonebook)

  Default value: `pb`

  Possible values:
  - `pb`:
    Main phonebook
  - `ich`:
    Incoming call history
  - `och`:
    Outgoing call history
  - `mch`:
    Missed call history
  - `cch`:
    Combined call history
  - `spd`:
    Speed-dial entries
  - `fav`:
    Favourites

* `--raw` — Show phone numbers as stored; skip E.164 normalisation. No effect on `--list`/`--sync`
* `--limit <N>` — Maximum contacts per page; omit to show all. No effect on `--sync`
* `--page <N>` — Page number (1-indexed). Ignored when `--limit` is not set. No effect on `--sync`

## `imsg sync`

Backfill the local store with all messages from the device since the last sync

**Usage:** `imsg sync [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--folder <FOLDER>` — Restrict the backfill to a single folder; omit to sync all folders

  Possible values:
  - `inbox`:
    Received messages
  - `sent`:
    Sent messages
  - `outbox`:
    Pending outbound messages
  - `deleted`:
    Deleted messages




## `imsg unsync`

Stop using the local store for reads; synced data is preserved by default

**Usage:** `imsg unsync [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--purge` — Delete the database file and all synced data in addition to disabling sync

## `imsg config`

**Usage:** `imsg config <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `set-device` — Persist the device MAC address to the user config file
* `setup` — Interactively pick a paired device, resolve its MAP/PBAP channels over SDP, and persist address + both channels together

## `imsg daemon`

Manage the persistent background broker (opt-in; required for GUI use)

**Usage:** `imsg daemon <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `start` — Start the persistent broker. Detaches into the background by default; idempotent if already running
* `stop` — Request a graceful stop. A no-op (not an error) if nothing is running
* `status` — Report whether the daemon is running and whether its MAP session is connected
* `install` — Register the daemon with the native OS service manager (systemd/launchd/OpenRC/ rc.d/sc.exe), so it starts on boot/login and restarts on failure. Optional — `imsg daemon start`/`stop` alone fully serve users who don't want OS-level supervision
* `uninstall` — Unregister the daemon service. A no-op if it was never installed



## `imsg daemon start`

Start the persistent broker. Detaches into the background by default; idempotent if already running

**Usage:** `imsg daemon start [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--foreground` — Stay attached instead of detaching — required under a process supervisor (e.g. a systemd unit). Stops on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or an IPC `Shutdown` request



## `imsg daemon stop`

Request a graceful stop. A no-op (not an error) if nothing is running

**Usage:** `imsg daemon stop`



## `imsg daemon status`

Report whether the daemon is running and whether its MAP session is connected

**Usage:** `imsg daemon status`



## `imsg daemon install`

Register the daemon with the native OS service manager (systemd/launchd/OpenRC/ rc.d/sc.exe), so it starts on boot/login and restarts on failure. Optional — `imsg daemon start`/`stop` alone fully serve users who don't want OS-level supervision

**Usage:** `imsg daemon install [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--system` — Register system-wide instead of for the current user only. Typically requires elevated privileges to install



## `imsg daemon uninstall`

Unregister the daemon service. A no-op if it was never installed

**Usage:** `imsg daemon uninstall [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--system` — Match the `--system`/user scope the service was installed with



## `imsg completions`

Print a shell completion script to stdout, or install it directly.

Without `--install`, redirect it into your shell's completion directory yourself, e.g. `imsg completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_imsg`.

**Usage:** `imsg completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<SHELL>` — Target shell

  Possible values: `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `powershell`, `zsh`


###### **Options:**

* `--install` — Write the script to the shell's conventional completion directory instead of printing it, after an interactive confirmation. Not supported for every shell
